title: Holtec Pioneer 2 (SMR-300 at Palisades): Enclosure 2: SMR-300 Instrumentation & Control Architecture Licensing Topical Report Audit Question Response Q-59 (Non-Proprietary) [['Response to Request for Additional Information (RAI)']]

documents.text:
NRC Audit for SMR-300 I&C Architecture LTR – Question No. 59                 [Date: 5/27/2026]

       The SMR-300 Plant Safety System (PSS) is a digital, safety-related Instrumentation and
       Control (I&C) system that provides automatic and manual control of safety functions and
       components. The PSS provides the primary interface for the operator to control safety
       equipment and perform post-accident monitoring system functions including reactor trip
       (RT) and Engineered Safety Feature (ESF) actuation. The topical report Section 3.3
       Control Stations describes control stations which include safety consoles with S-VDU
       (Safety Visual Display Unit), a Manual Initiation switch and the master transfer switch
       installed in both Main Control Room (MCR) and Remote Shutdown Facility (RSF) which
       are all supported by the PSS. Does the design of the architecture described in the
       topical report present any constraints on the information that can be presented on the
       Human System Interface (HSI) due to sensor data availability?

       [Guidance Reference: NUREG 0711 – Section 8 HSI Design Inputs I&C System
       Requirements (8.4.1 HSI Design Inputs)]


SMR Response                                                                  [Date: 6/8/2026]

The information presented on the PSS HSI is based on the safety-related process, status, and
actuation information that is acquired, processed, and transmitted through predefined PSS
signal paths.

The PSS includes four redundant and independent instrumentation channels. Each channel
receives dedicated sensor inputs that are processed by its associated channel bistable
processor (CBP). The CBPs transmit bistable outputs and instrument monitoring information to
the reactor protection processors (RPPs) through [[                           ]]. The RPPs
then provide monitoring information to the S-VDU over [[                          ]]. Within
each division, [[
                                                                         ]].

Accordingly, the S-VDU can present the safety-related information made available through the
PSS architecture, including process value monitoring, safety related post-accident monitoring
(PAM), alarm status monitoring, bypass and inoperable status indication, component status, and
information associated with manual operation or initiation functions. The architecture does not
impose a sensor-data-availability constraint on the presentation of predefined safety-related
PSS information on the S-VDU.
